idea-plugin.description:
Opens Wi-Fi Channel State Information captures written in the CSIQ interchange format, and the raw driver streams they are derived from, as a visual editor inside any IntelliJ-based IDE.

  • Waterfall - amplitude over subcarrier and time, across the whole capture, with zoom down to individual records. The time axis shows wall clock, elapsed time, or the host's own stamps, and the wall clock is anchored once and then advanced by the baseband clock, which an NTP step cannot move.
  • Spectrum - one record's amplitude and phase per tone, per chain, with a chain that reported no measurement marked as such.
  • Impulse response - the channel impulse response and the inter-chain conjugate product, with the early-to-late energy ratio that tells you whether the coefficients were read in the right order.
  • Records - every record's clocks, RSSI, PHY label, source MAC and geometry, read from an index rather than from the file.
  • Fields and bytes - each TLV with the specification's own wording for what it means, the 272-byte driver header decoded at its documented offsets, and a hex view.
  • Session - the embedded session block, and what the capture says about itself: rate, dropped reports, all-zero records, stale chains, and how the stream ended.

Formats. .csiq, .csiq.zst and capture.raw. A compressed container is expanded once into a local cache, because the specification compresses the file and never the format.

Remote captures. Every byte is read through the platform's virtual file system, never through a filesystem path, so a capture on S3, HDFS or SFTP mounted by Big Data Tools or Remote File Systems opens exactly like a local one. Neither plugin is required, and this one declares no dependency on either.

action.description: Open a .csiq, .csiq.zst or capture.raw file, local or remote
